I got the opportunity to visit the CSIR National Institute of Data Science and AI (CSIR-4PI), Bengaluru. The institute comes under the CSIR - National Aerospace Laboratories (NAL) and is well known for its work in advanced computing and interdisciplinary research. It provides high-performance computing facilities that support studies in areas like climate modelling, biology, space science, and information technology.

The visit took place on the occasion of the institute’s 84th Foundation Day. The idea behind this event was to spread awareness about the research happening there and to give us real exposure to the latest technologies being developed.

Witnessed several remarkable research initiatives across diverse scientific domains:

> Cyber Security – The session provided in-depth insights into threat intelligence, demonstrating how data packets are analyzed and captured to identify and prevent potential security breaches.
> Agro-Technology – Showcased how innovation is revolutionizing modern agricultural practices with the help of advanced scientific instruments .
> High Performance Computing (HPC) Facility – A supercomputing facility, named as 'Ananta' is recognized as one of the top supercomputers in the country and is one of the flagship activities of CSIR-4PI.

The visit was highly insightful and served as a motivation to further explore these technologies and their real-world applications.

A few days ago, our team ResolveX successfully submitted the prototype for the second stage of the Smart India Hackathon 2025💡. This journey was much more than just a hackathon project. It was a true test of our consistency and teamwork. From meeting project deadlines to organizing brainstorming sessions, we worked hard to transform our idea into a meaningful and functional prototype 🛠.

🌟 I had the opportunity to lead our team of six under the problem statement 'Identification of Infrastructure, Amenities, and Service Gaps in SC-Majority Villages for Adarsh Gram Declaration', proposed by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment (MoSJE) 💡.

Though we faced an unexpected challenge — a delay in receiving credentials that caused our upload slot to fill before submission, we chose to take it as a learning experience rather than a setback. It motivated us to refine our concept and build an even stronger prototype under a new problem statement 🚀.

This experience truly reflected our team’s resilience and determination in handling last-minute hurdles with positivity.

I’m grateful to my incredible teammates for their dedication and collaborative spirit. Together, we proved that challenges can become the foundation for something even greater ✨.

🚨 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐩 '𝐀𝐥𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐀𝐥𝐥': 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐜𝐞𝐥 𝐈𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐓𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬 𝐔𝐬

We love the speed of the instant deployment economy, but we’ve become far too comfortable with the '𝗔𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗔𝗹𝗹' button. In 2026, 𝗢𝗔𝘂𝘁𝗵 tokens are high-value credentials and the [**Vercel**](https://www.linkedin.com/company/vercel/) breach is an eye-opener in how attackers are now using them to walk through the front door.

🔍 But here is the reality: This didn't start with a complex code injection. It was a supply chain attack via a third-party AI tool called [**Context.ai**](http://context.ai/).

Nowadays, Agentic AI and SaaS integrations are the new attack surfaces. So when you click 'Allow All' on that new tool, you might be handing over the keys to your entire infrastructure.

💡𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗶𝗴 𝗟𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗼𝗻 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗗𝗲𝘃𝘀 & 𝗦𝘁𝘂𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀

Modern security isn't just about your code, it's about your permissions. So let's stop treating OAuth tokens as temporary logins because they are high-value credentials.

⭐️ The takeaway? We don’t need to stop using these tools, but we do need to stop giving them 'Allow All' permissions by default.

Attending this summit was more than just another tech event. It felt like witnessing a shift in how we build, think and innovate.

We’ve seen waves before like cloud, big data, early AI. But what stood out this time wasn’t just the advancement of AI, it was how seamlessly it’s becoming part of real world decision-making. Amidst all the noise, a clear sense of purpose is taking shape.

The highlight was definitely the keynote session, watching industry experts delivering powerful insights on next-gen infrastructure and production-ready agentic AI workflows.

• [**Satinder Singh**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/satinder-singh-1678b73/) Director, Solutions Architecture, AWS India
Kicked off the keynote session and demonstrated how AI workloads are pushing the limits of traditional infrastructure. He unveiled the latest Trainium3 3 nm chip and Graviton4 processor and showcased the live demonstration of controlling the actions using brain signals diving into Bedrock AgentCore.

• [**Olivier Klein**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kleinolivier/) Chief Technologist, AWS
Talked in depth about the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore explaining the entire architecture with model capabilities and infrastructure layers.

• [**Murali Swaminathan**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/muraliswaminathan/) CTO, Freshworks
Delivered how they’re transforming the post- AI era in collaboration with AWS by building reusable Al integrations across the enterprise.

• [**Pratyush Kumar**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pratyush-kumar-8844a8a3/) Co-founder, Sarvam AI
• [**Rishi Bal**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rishibal/) CEO, BharatGen
Showcased the commitment to [**hashtag#BuildForBharat**](https://www.linkedin.com/search/results/all/?keywords=%23buildforbharat&origin=HASH_TAG_FROM_FEED) with their Gen AI platforms and shared impressive benchmarks of their LLMs.

• [**Mudit Agrawal**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/agrawalmudit/) Senior Applied Science Manager, Amazon Robotics
Presented Amazon’s Vulcan robot which is enhancing the warehouse efficiency with advanced touch technology.

The real takeaway?

Spent an insightful day at GitHub Copilot Dev Days @ [**Microsoft**](https://www.linkedin.com/company/microsoft/) Prestige Ferns Office, Bengaluru.

A day packed with real learning, hands-on demos and meaningful conversations around AI.

From understanding how LLMs actually work to seeing real-world DevOps workflows powered by Copilot, the sessions made one thing clear:
👉 The future of coding is co-creation, not automation.

⭐️ Key takeaways:
—> The focus is moving from concepts to real, usable workflows
—> AI is shifting from support to active collaboration in development
—> Human judgment remains essential as AI supports, not replaces
